In the [[mathematics|mathematical]] field of [[complex analysis]], '''Akhiezer's theorem''' is a result about [[entire function]]s proved by [[Naum Akhiezer]].<ref>see {{harvtxt|Akhiezer|1948}}.</ref>

==Statement==
Let <math>f:\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{C}</math> be an [[entire function]] of [[exponential type]] <math>\tau</math>, with <math>f(x)\geq 0</math> for real <math>x</math>. Then the following are equivalent:

* There exists an [[entire function]] <math>F</math>, of [[exponential type]] <math>\tau/2</math>, having all its zeros in the (closed) upper half plane, such that

:: <math>f(z)=F(z)\overline{F(\overline{z})}</math>

* One has:

::<math>
\sum_n |\operatorname{Im}(1/z_{n})|<\infty
</math>
where <math>z_n</math> are the zeros of <math>f</math>.

==Related results==
It is not hard to show that the [[Fejér–Riesz theorem]] is a special case.<ref>see {{harvtxt|Boas|1954}} and {{harvtxt|Boas|1944}} for references.</ref>
